RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
The ten remaining accused appeared on remand
before the 1st. S.S.D.Court during the morning of the
9th. July, 1937, when the following judgment was
rendered : -
1st. & 2nd. accused - 7 months impt.
4th. accused - 1 ½ years impt.
16th. accused - 6 months impt. or fined at
the rate of $2 per day.
14th. and 15th. accused - 6 ½ years impt. each.
3rd. accused - 8 years impt.
12 th accused - 3 years impt.
5th. and 10th. accused - Not guilty.
The pistols, ammunition, counterfeiting para-
phernalia were ordered to be confiscated, and handed over
temporarily to the Headquarters of the Shanghai & Woosung
Garrison Commander.
The ten remaining prisoners were then ordered to
be handed over to the above authorities for further
investigation regarding their political activities.

其余十名被告于1937年7月9日上午在第二特区地方法院（1st. S.S.D. Court）出庭受审，判决如下：

第十六被告 - 监禁6个月，或按每日2元之标准罚款。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Instead of this case coming before the Court on the 29th. June, 1937, the Judge postponed the hearing until the 2nd. July, 1937. On this date, the accused persons appeared before Judge Feng, when in addition to the charges enumerated in the previous report, application was made by a representative of the Shanghai & Woosung Garrison Commander for the extradition of all the accused on charges relating to their subversive activities. As no charges had been preferred against the 6th. 7th. 8th. 9th. 11th. 13th. 18th. 19th. and 20th. accused, the Judge ordered that the 6th. 11th. 13th. 18th 19th. and 20th. accused be forthwith extradited to the Chinese authorities, whilst the four females, the 7th. 8th. 9th. and 17th. accused be released. The trial of the 1st. 2nd. 3rd. 4th. 5th. 10th. 12th. 14th. 15th. and 16th. accused was concluded the same afternoon.
Judgment in respect of these persons will be rendered on the 9th. July, 1937, after which they will be extradited to the Headquarters of the Shanghai & Woosung Garrison Commander.
（印：SPECIAL ... 3 JULY 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
SECRET
File No. 7975
C.B., H.Q. /Shalibi,
REPORT
Date June 24 1937.

Subject Statement made by Li Hsi Ling and others, and translation of documents.

Made by D.S.I. Coyne Forwarded by

Forwarded herewith are statements made by:
Li Hsi Ling (李麟), 11th accused;
Hsu Ts Ming (徐志敏), 12th accused;
Ting Kau Sz (丁高氏) 8th accused, wife of 4th accused;
Yang Zung Sz (楊盛氏) 7th accused, wife of 6th accused;
Zau Yoong Sz (趙榮氏) 17th accused, wife of 16th accused;
Yang Dien Wo (楊典華) 6th accused (2nd statement);
also a translation of two documents found in the home of Yang
Dien Wo (楊典華) and a tabulated list of the persons in custody,
showing their connection with criminal cases and the Young
Military Men's Society.

On June 22, representatives of the Garrison Commander
briefly questioned Yang Dien Wo, Zau Koh Hwa, Ting Zeu Daung
and Li Hsi Ling after which they stated that at the next hearing
of the case an application would be made by the Chinese Authori-
ties for the extradition of all the persons now in the custody
of the Police in connection with this case.

From the statements made by Ting Zeu Daung, Yang Dien
Wo, Zau Koh Hwa, Li Hsi Ling and Hsu Ts Ming, there appears to
be grounds for the application for their custody by the Chinese
Authorities. There is no evidence to indicate at this stage
that the remainder of those in custody have engaged in any
political or subversive activity.

A summary of this case will be prepared on completion
of proceedings at the S.S.D. Court.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 24 JUNE 1937 CRIME BRANCH）
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH 25 JUNE 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

Received.
by Information Bureau
Forwarded to S.S.D.
J. Logan
D.S.I.

日期 1937年6月24日。

主题 李麟等人所作陈述及文件译文。

由副督察 Coyne 制作 转呈者

随函附上以下人员所作陈述：
李麟 (Li Hsi Ling)，第十一被告；
徐志敏 (Hsu Ts Ming)，第十二被告；
丁高氏 (Ting Kau Sz)，第八被告，第四被告之妻；
楊盛氏 (Yang Zung Sz)，第七被告，第六被告之妻；
趙榮氏 (Zau Yoong Sz)，第十七被告，第十六被告之妻；
楊典華 (Yang Dien Wo)，第六被告（第二次陈述）；
另附在楊典華 (Yang Dien Wo) 家中发现的两份文件的译文，以及一份在押人员列表，显示其与刑事案件及青年军人社（Young Military Men's Society）的关联。

6月22日，要塞司令部代表简要讯问了楊典華、赵国华 (Zau Koh Hwa)、丁祖堂 (Ting Zeu Daung) 和李麟，随后他们表示，在下次开庭审理此案时，中国当局将申请引渡目前因本案被警方羁押的所有人员。

从丁祖堂、楊典華、赵国华、李麟和徐志敏所作的陈述来看，中国当局申请羁押他们是有理由的。现阶段没有证据表明其余在押人员参与了任何政治或颠覆活动。

待第二特区地方法院诉讼程序结束后，将编制本案摘要。

（印章：副总监 1937年6月24日 刑事股）
（印章：特别股 1937年6月25日 上海公共租界工部局警务处）

情报局收悉。
转呈第二特区地方法院。
J. Logan
副督察。

Chief of the Kiangsu Group of the Young Military
Men's Society organised by the late Mr. Hu Han
Min. After the latter's death, the society was
controlled by Liu Loo Ying; Liu is at present
serving a term of imprisonment for being concern-
ed in the murder of the late Gen. Yang Yung Tai,
formerly governor of Hupeh Province. A search
of his home at 260 Rue Lafayette resulted in the
seizure of a number of documents, including a
letter of appointment from Liu Loo Ying, a map
showing the distribution of military units in
Kiangsu and two lists showing the strength of the
Paotui, Water Police, Police and Merchants
Volunteer Corps in various hsiens in Kiangsu.

Arrested in room No.42 Saung Kiang (長江)
Lodging House, No.2 Av. Rd. VII, on informa-
tion supplied by the 3rd accused.
In his possession was found a parcel of
metal fragments which he states were intended
for the manufacture of a bomb. In his room
were also found three plaster of paris dies
for the manufacture of counterfeit coins.
According to the accused the bomb was to
be made by one named Van Min (范敏)
residing at No.11 Loh Dau Tsung, Daung Wei
Shian Village, 6 li off Minghong. This
address was raided with the assistance of
the Chinese authorities and 8 rounds of
ammunition and several summonses as well
as a written judgment were seized.
The verdict shows that Van Min alias Kao
Tse Ping, alias Van Sz Yung, alias Van Sz
Yeong was twice arrested by the Chinese
authorities, once in 1930 on a charge of
robbery, again in 1933 on a charge of being
a communist. For the latter offence Van
was sentenced on 5/8/33 to three years'
imprisonment by the Kiangsu High Court.
At the time of the raid Van was absent
and efforts to locate him have so far been
unsuccessful.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of 11th accused Li Hsi Ling (李錫麟)
native of Hsuchow. taken by me D.S.I. Coyne
at C.B.H.Q. on the 19.6.37. and interpreted by D.S.I. Shih.

My name is Li Hsi Lin, (李錫麟) I was born at Soochow
in 1913, my father Li Yue Tsung (李雨村), who is in the army,
being a native of Hsuchow. He is now with the 52nd Army at
Lung Zee Hsien, Chekiang.
Between the ages of six and 19 I attended school, the
last year being at the Futan University Middle School, and the
previous two years at the Kading Junior Middle School. As a
student I did not participate in any political activities, or
make a study of communism or sociology.
On leaving school I joined my father at Wuchang, he then
being employed as a clerk at the Military Acedemy. Being unable
to obtain employment I returned to Hsuchow, and a few months
later, in 1933, I joined the Revenue 税警 Guards Training School, and
after a three month course was posted to Pootung. I was later
sent to the Officers' Training School at Sung Kiang for a three
months course and after passing was posted to Tse Hwa, Lisho.
(瀏河七丁口). After being there for ten months, at the end
of 1934 I was appointed Deputy Chief of a special squad raised
to deal with salt smugglers, who had killed several guards.
One named Liu Chi Wei (劉志會), a Sub-Inspector of
the Water Police at Liehuo in March 1936 told me of the existence
of an organization headed by Mr. Hu Han Ming, and suggested that
I join it as it was probable that Hun Han would get into power
and members of his organ-ization would be able to get good
positions.
I agreed to his suggestion and he took me to the Sing
Xie Lu Sau Hotel (新旅社), Kingtang Road, and there introduced

以下为第11名被告李锡麟（Li Hsi Ling），徐州人，于1937年6月19日在中央捕房总部（C.B.H.Q.）由副督察长科因（D.S.I. Coyne）录取，并由副督察长施（D.S.I. Shih）翻译的供词。

我叫李锡麟（Li Hsi Lin），1913年生于苏州，父亲李雨村（Li Yue Tsung），徐州人，在军队服役。他目前随第五十二军在浙江龙溪县（Lung Zee Hsien）（音译）。
六岁至十九岁期间我就读于学校，最后一年在复旦大学中学部，前两年在嘉定初级中学。作为学生，我没有参与任何政治活动，也没有研究共产主义或社会学。
离校后，我去武昌投奔父亲，他当时在军校担任书记员。因无法找到工作，我回到徐州，几个月后，即1933年，我加入了税警训练学校，经过三个月的课程后被派往浦东。后来我被派往松江军官训练学校参加三个月的课程，通过后被派往浏河七丁口（Tse Hwa, Lisho）。在那里十个月后，于1934年底，我被任命为专门对付杀害数名警卫的盐枭的特勤队副队长。
1936年3月，一名叫刘志会（Liu Chi Wei）的人，烈浒（Liehuo）（音译）水上警察局的副巡官，告诉我有一个以胡汉民先生为首的组织存在，并建议我加入，因为胡汉很可能掌权，其组织成员将获得好职位。
我同意了他的建议，他带我到金堂路（Kingtang Road）的新旅社（Sing Xie Lu Sau Hotel），并在那里介绍

native of....................................................taken by me....................................................

me to one named Tsang Soong Liang (張重良). Tsang told me
that the Young Military Men's Party was formed by Mr. Hu Han
Ming and controlled by Mr. Liu Loo Ying, its policy was, briefly
Anti-Japanese, Anti-Communist, Anti-Blueshirt and Anti-Dictator.
When I told Tsang that I was willing to join the Party
he telephoned to Yang Dien Wo (6th accused) who came to the
hotel. Yang repeated the explanation given me by Tsang
regarding the object of the Party, and then I signed a pledge
form by which I became a member of the Party.
I was instructed by Yang to try to get more members for
the Party, but I was unable to do so.
In May 1936, I met Yang in the home of Liu Chi Wei at 3,
Hung Nyung Li, Route de Marche (華木路鴻寧里), and he then told
me that as I had received a good education it was his intention
to send me to Hongkong to attend a six months course at the
training school of the Young Military Mens Party, after which
I would be appointed a district officer at a salary of $100
per month. He then instructed me to resign from the Revenue
Guard and hold myself in readiness to proceed to Hongkong. I
carried out his instructions and removed to 27 B. Jessfield
Road, where I resided for three months, but hearing nothing
about going to Hongkong, and being without money, I went to
stay with my mother at Kading.
Periodically I came to Shanghai to see Yang, and on the
day I was arrested I had been here about one month, staying
with a friend named Xia Xiang Shing (謝祥興) at the Sing
Sung Wo Lodging House (新生活), French Concession. With

我认识一位名叫张重良（Tsang Soong Liang）的人。张告诉我，青年军人党由胡汉民先生组建，由刘罗英（Liu Loo Ying）（音译）先生控制，其政策简而言之是反日、反共、反蓝衣社和反独裁。
当我告诉张我愿意入党时，他打电话给杨殿武（Yang Dien Wo）（第6名被告），杨来到旅馆。杨重复了张关于该党目标的解释，然后我签署了一份誓愿书，从而成为该党党员。
杨指示我试图为该党发展更多成员，但我未能做到。
1936年5月，我在刘志会位于华木路鸿宁里3号的家中遇见杨，他当时告诉我，鉴于我受过良好教育，他打算送我去香港参加青年军人党训练学校为期六个月的课程，之后我将被任命为区级官员，月薪100元。随后他指示我辞去税警职务，并做好准备前往香港。我执行了他的指示，搬至杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）27B号，在那里住了三个月，但因未听到去香港的消息，且身无分文，我便去嘉定与母亲同住。
我定期来上海见杨，在我被捕当天，我已在此约一个月，住在法租界新生活旅馆（Sing Sung Wo Lodging House）的一位名叫谢祥兴（Xia Xiang Shing）的朋友处。怀着

The following is the statement of 12th accused Hsu Ts Ming (徐老敏).
native of Minghong, Kiangsu taken by me D.S.I. Coyne.
at C.B., H.Q. on the 22.6.37. and interpreted by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien

My name is Hsu Ts Ming, age 29, native of Minghong.
My address was, prior to my arrest, Room No. 42 Shaung Kiang
Hotel, No. 2 Edward Avenue VII, French Concession.
My father Hsu Foh-chong is a newspaper vendor by
profession and has no fixed abode. I don't know where
he is living now.
I entered the Tsong Jao Primary School, Minghong, when
I was eight years of age, and later attended the Minghong
Normal School. I discontinued my study in 1922 when I was
14 years old owing to financial difficulties. At this juncture
a friend of mine named Zee Kwong Foh (徐光福) persuaded me
to join the Communist Party and I did. He gave me two pieces
of cloth, one red and the other black in colour, with instruc-
tion to fasten the red cloth inside my sleeve and the black
one outside it as a sign of being a communist. I don't know
what position Zee held in the Communist Party. He didn't
bring me to see anybody nor did he bring me any communistic
books to read. I didn't draw any salary or allowance from
Zee. Sometimes Zee instructed me to write a number of slogans
on paper slips which Zee later posted in the street. The
wording of the slogans written was as follows:-
"Peasants, unite together and rise up!
Workers, unite together and rise up!
Merchants, unite together and rise up!
Support the Communist Party!
Down with the Imperialists!"
I withdrew from the Communist Party about a year later

以下为第12名被告徐老敏（Hsu Ts Ming），江苏闵行人的供词，由副督察长科因（D.S.I. Coyne）于1937年6月22日在中央捕房总部（C.B., H.Q.）录取，并由副督察长施思坚（D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien）翻译。

我叫徐老敏，29岁，闵行人。被捕前的住址是法租界爱德华七世路2号双江旅馆42号房间。
我的父亲徐佛崇（Hsu Foh-chong）（音译）职业是报贩，没有固定住所。我不知道他现在住在哪里。
我八岁时进入闵行忠孝小学（Tsong Jao Primary School）（音译），后来就读于闵行师范学校。1922年，我14岁时，因经济困难辍学。此时，我的一位名叫徐光福（Zee Kwong Foh）的朋友劝我加入共产党，我便加入了。他给了我两块布，一块红色，另一块黑色，指示我将红布缝在袖子里面，黑布缝在外面，作为共产党员的标志。我不知道徐在共产党中担任什么职务。他没有带我去见任何人，也没有给我任何共产主义书籍阅读。我没有从徐那里领取任何薪水或津贴。有时徐指示我在纸条上写一些标语，徐后来将这些标语张贴在街上。所写标语的内容如下：
“农民们，团结起来起义！
工人们，团结起来起义！
商人们，团结起来起义！
支持共产党！
打倒帝国主义！”
大约一年后我退出了共产党

when I was 16 years of age because I was disgusted with the

In 1926 I came to Shanghai and earned my living by
drawing portraits. I had no fixed abode but resided at
various lodging houses.
On May 19, 1937 I removed my home from No.37 Kong Ka
Zah, Tseu Kah Jao (周家橋龔家宅), O.O.L. to Room No.42,
Shaung Kiang Hotel, No.2 Avenue Edward VII, French Concession.
At about 11 a.m. on June 14, one named Van Ming (范敏), a
school mate of mine, came to my home and placed into my
custody a small leather suitcase. He didn't tell me what it
contained but stated that he would return for it later.
At about 2 p.m. on the same day, the 3rd accused, Li Zang Sung
whom I don't know and have never seen before, led a party of
police came to my room with a view to apprehending Van Ming.
As Van Ming was absent, I was arrested.
Van Ming is a clerk in the employ of lawyer Yao Nyi
Piau (姚彝標), Rue Bourgeat, French Concession. I don't
know if he is a communist. I don't know whether the suitcase
contained something for making a bomb.

当时我16岁，因为我厌恶共产党的学说。
1926年我来到上海，以画肖像为生。我没有固定住所，而是居住在各个旅馆。
1937年5月19日，我将家从越界筑路周家桥龚家宅37号搬至法租界爱德华七世路2号双江旅馆42号房间。
6月14日上午11点左右，一位名叫范敏（Van Ming）的同学来到我家，将一个小皮箱交给我保管。他没有告诉我里面装了什么，但说以后会回来取。
同日下午2点左右，第3名被告李藏松（Li Zang Sung）（音译），我不认识也从未见过此人，带领一队警察来到我的房间，旨在逮捕范敏。由于范敏不在，我被捕。
范敏是法租界蒲石路（Rue Bourgeat）律师姚彝标（Yao Nyi Piau）的雇员。我不知道他是否是共产党员。我不知道皮箱里是否装有制造炸弹的物品。

The following is the statement of Ting Kao Sz (丁高氏)
native of Kiangpeh taken by me D.S.I. Coyne
at Police Hqrs. on the 21/6/37 and interpreted by Clerk Liao.

My name is Ting Kao Sz. I am 24 years of age, native
of Kiangpeh. Ting Zeu Sung is my paramour. We were not
legally married. I made the acquaintance of Ting in Haiming
in 1936 when Ting was employed with the Opium Suppression
Superintendent's Office, Haimung. My parents are still alive;
they are operating a barbers shop in Haimung.

The Opium Suppression Superintendent's Office, Haimung,
was abolished in August 1936 when I and Ting came to Shanghai,
he intending to find a job here. Ever since our arrival we
have been residing in an upstairs room of House No.64 Zee Zung
Li, Rue Brenier de Montmorand, the rentals being $5.50 per
mensem.

In Shanghai Ting failed to secure employment. He received
each month about $10 from his two uncles, one of whom is
employed at a poulterers shop in Nantao, the other at a pig
hong. The sum was hardly sufficient to pay for our food.
Consequently we were unable to pay our rent for the past 9
months.

Ting used to go to see his uncles and friends during the
day. I don't know any of Ting's friends except one Li Kwei
Sung (李桂生) who was an office-mate of Ting while the latter
was employed with the Opium Suppression Superintendent's office
in Haimung.

As I and Ting are not legally married, Ting did not con-
verse with me about his private affairs. I knew he had been
married but his wife had died.

Mrs. Yang who is a teacher of the Kwan Chi Primary School,

以下为丁高氏（Ting Kao Sz），江北人的供词，由副督察长科因（D.S.I. Coyne）于1937年6月21日在警察总局录取，并由职员廖翻译。

我叫丁高氏。我24岁，江北人。丁祖松（Ting Zeu Sung）（音译）是我的情夫。我们没有合法结婚。1936年我在海门认识了丁，当时丁在海门禁烟局任职。我的父母尚在人世；他们在海门经营一家理发店。

海门禁烟局于1936年8月撤销，当时我和丁来到上海，他打算在这里找工作。自我们抵达以来，一直居住在白利南路芝宗里64号的一间楼上房间，租金为每月5.50元。

丁在上海未能找到工作。他每月从他的两个叔叔那里收到约10元，其中一个在南市的一家家禽店工作，另一个在一家猪行工作。这笔钱几乎不够支付我们的食物费用。因此，我们在过去9个月里无法支付房租。

丁白天常去看望他的叔叔和朋友。除了李桂生（Li Kwei Sung）以外，我不认识丁的任何朋友，李是丁在海门禁烟局任职时的同事。

由于我和丁没有合法结婚，丁不与我谈论他的私事。我知道他结过婚，但他的妻子已经去世。

杨女士是关之小学（Kwan Chi Primary School）（音译）的教师，

Rue Paul Beau, often came to see our 1st tenant, an old woman, whose two grand-daughters are studying in the school in question. I and Mrs. Yang later became friends but I don't know her husband.

On June 11, Li Kwei Sung came to my home and told me that Ting was staying in a room in the Sing San Kiang Lodging House, Canton Road, and would not return for a few days because he intended to evade payment of debts on the approaching Dragon Boat Festival (June 13).

I went to the Lodging House to see Ting at noon on June 11. At the entrance of the alleyway (Zee Zung Li), I met Mrs. Yang who told me that she had some trouble with her husband and did not want to stay at her home. I advised her to come with me to the lodging house to which she agreed.

When we arrived at the lodging house we saw Ting Zeu Daung, Li Kwei Sung, Zung Zu Tseng, and her husband named Tung in the room. Tung has returned to his native place in Kiangpeh.

On June 14 I was arrested together with the other persons by the Police in the Lodging House. I don't know why I was arrested.

(Signed) Ting Kao Sz.

博伟路（Rue Paul Beau），常来探望我们的第一号租客，一位老妇人，她的两个孙女正在上述学校读书。我和杨太太后来成了朋友，但我不认识她的丈夫。

6月11日，李桂生（Li Kwei Sung）来到我家，告诉我丁某住在广东路新三江旅馆的一个房间里，因打算逃避即将到来的端午节（6月13日）的债务，几天内不会回来。

6月11日中午，我去旅馆见丁某。在弄堂（芝宗里，Zee Zung Li）入口处，我遇到了杨太太，她告诉我她与丈夫有些矛盾，不想待在家里。我建议她随我去旅馆，她同意了。

当我们到达旅馆时，我们在房间里看到了丁佐唐（Ting Zeu Daung）、李桂生、钟祖曾（Zung Zu Tseng）以及她的丈夫童某。童某已返回其江北老家。

6月14日，我与旅馆内的其他人一起被警察逮捕。我不知道为何被捕。

（签名）丁高氏（Ting Kao Sz）。

The following is the statement of...7th accused Yang Zung Sz alias Zung Yan Pih..
native of....Chingpoo Hsien, Kiangsu,.....taken by me..D.S.I. Coyne
at....C.B., H.Q........on the....21.6.37............and interpreted by...D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien

My name is Yang Zung Sz, alias Zung Yan Pih (楊盛氏/盛快碧)
age 31 years, native of Chingpoo Hsien, Kiangsu. Prior to my
arrest, I was residing with my husband Yang Dien Wo at No.260
Rue Lafayette, French Concession.
My father was an employee of the Peiping-Hankow Railway
and he died in the year 1917.
I began my education in the Tsingpoo Primary School,
Tsingpoo, when I was 9 years of age. When I graduated from
the above school at the age of 17, I went to Sungkiang and
studied one year in the Sungkiang Normal School.
Through the introduction of a priest named Yao Ping
Hsuen (姚秉), I was married to my husband at Chingpoo
Hsien in 1927 when he was holding a position as the Chief of
the 1st Division of the Chingpoo Police Bureau. I knew nothing
of my husband before our marriage, except that he had been a
military officer under General Chien Dah Chuen (錢大鈞).
About one year after our marriage, my husband resigned
his position owing to illness and we went to Nanking. Several
months later my husband recovered from his illness and was
re-appointed to the same position, and we again returned to
Chingpoo. He held this position for another year and again
resigned, the reason for which I now can't remember.
We came to Shanghai in 1930 with our daughter who was
then two years old. Since then my husband occasionally left
Shanghai for Nanking, Kiangse and other ports in search of
employment, but I was left behind staying at No.52 (?) Woo Foh
Lee off Rue Pere Froc, French Concession.

以下为...第七被告杨盛氏，别名盛快碧..
籍贯....江苏青浦县，.....由本人..副督察员科因（D.S.I. Coyne）
于....中央捕房总部........在....1937年6月21日............录取，并由...副督察员施思坚（D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien）翻译

我叫杨盛氏，别名盛快碧（楊盛氏/盛快碧），
31岁，江苏青浦县人。在被捕前，我与丈夫杨殿沃（Yang Dien Wo）居住在法租界辣斐德路260号。
我的父亲是平汉铁路的职员，于1917年去世。
我9岁时开始在青浦小学接受教育。17岁从上述学校毕业后，我去了松江，在松江师范学校学习了一年。
通过一位名叫姚秉轩（Yao Ping Hsuen，姚秉）的神父介绍，我于1927年在青浦县与丈夫结婚，当时他担任青浦警察局第一分局局长。婚前我对丈夫一无所知，只知道他曾是钱大钧将军手下的一名军官。
婚后约一年，丈夫因病辞职，我们去了南京。几个月后，丈夫病愈，被重新任命为同一职位，我们又回到了青浦。他在这个职位上又干了一年，再次辞职，原因我现在记不起来了。
1930年，我们带着当时两岁的女儿来到上海。此后，丈夫偶尔离开上海去南京、江西和其他港口寻找工作，但我留在后面，住在法租界神父路（Rue Pere Froc）附近的武定里52号（?）。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Yang Zung Sz
native of taken by me
at on the and interpreted by

Immediately after the Shanghai Incident in 1932 my husband went to Jehol engaged in anti-Japanese activities and returned to Shanghai about 9 months later. I only knew that he was in command of the 8th Route Volunteer Army but I am not familiar with the detail of his activities. My husband very seldom discussed his business with me, and I was also too busy on my domestic affairs to meddle with his.

Upon his return to Shanghai from Jehol, my husband was unemployed for quite a long time, and then I heard that he had joined the late Mr. Hu Han Ming's party, the name of which I don't know. He went to Hongkong once about two years ago, but I don't remember the exact date and the object of his trip.

I know a number of my husband's friends among whom were Zau Koh Hwa (16th accused), Li Hsi Ling (11th accused), Tsang Soong Liang, Mah Kyi and etc. who were regular visitors to our house. I don't know Ting Zeu Daung.

After my husband joined Hu Han Ming's party, he usually gave me some $60 per month for family expenses, but he was unable to do so after October, 1936 and he did not explain why. Since then we have lived by pawning our belongings.

In January 1937 I became a school teacher in the Kwang Chi Primary School, Rue Wantz (光启路广慈小学), but I resigned this position about a fortnight later owing to illness. It was during this period that I gained the acquaintance of Ting Kau Sz (8th accused, wife of the 4th accused Ting Zeu Daung) who often escorted several children of her friends to the said school.

以下为杨盛氏之陈述
籍贯 由本人
于 在 录取，并由 翻译

1932年一·二八事变发生后不久，我丈夫前往热河从事抗日活动，约9个月后回到上海。我只知道他指挥第八路志愿军，但不熟悉他活动的细节。我丈夫很少与我讨论他的事务，我也忙于家务，无暇过问他的事。

丈夫从热河回到上海后，失业了很长一段时间，后来我听说他加入了已故胡汉民先生的党派，具体名称我不知道。大约两年前他去了一次香港，但我不记得确切日期和此行目的。

我认识丈夫的一些朋友，其中包括赵国华（Zau Koh Hwa，第16被告）、李希龄（Li Hsi Ling，第11被告）、张重良（Tsang Soong Liang）、马奇（Mah Kyi）等，他们是家里的常客。我不认识丁佐唐。

丈夫加入胡汉民的党派后，通常每月给我约60元作为家用，但1936年10月后他无法再这样做，也没有解释原因。此后我们靠典当物品为生。

1937年1月，我在万兹路（Rue Wantz，光启路）广慈小学成为一名教师，但因病约两周后辞职。正是在这期间，我结识了丁高氏（Ting Kau Sz，第8被告，第4被告丁佐唐之妻），她经常护送几位朋友的孩子到该校。

The following is the statement of Yeng Zung Sz
native of taken by me
at on the and interpreted by
On June 11, I had a quarrel with my husband because
of financial difficulties and I left my home with my daughter.
I intended to visit Ting Kau Sz at her home at No.64 Si Zung
Lee, Rue Grenier Montmorand, but I met her at the mouth of
the said alleyway. Ting Kau Sz told me that she had engaged
a room in the Sing San Kiang Lodging house, Canton Road, with
the object of avoiding the debt collectors during the Dragon
Festival. I accompanied her to the lodging house and stayed
there with her. My husband came to the lodging house three
times urging me to return home with him, but I refused. On
June 14 I was arrested by the Municipal Police.
This is my true statement.

6月11日，我因经济困难与丈夫争吵，便带着女儿离家出走。我本打算去蒙托邦路（Rue Grenier Montmorand）芝宗里64号丁高氏家拜访她，但在该弄堂口遇到了她。丁高氏告诉我，为了在端午节期间躲避债主，她在广东路新三江旅馆租了一个房间。我陪她去了旅馆，并和她住在一起。我丈夫三次来到旅馆催促我跟他回家，但我拒绝了。6月14日，我被工部局警察逮捕。
这是我的真实陈述。

The following is the statement of 17th accused Zau Yoong Sz 趙熊氏,
native of Kompo. taken by me D.S.I. Coyne
at J.B., H.Q. on the 21.6.37 and interpreted by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien

My name is Zau Yoong Sz (趙熊氏), age 29, native of
Kompo. I reside with my husband Zau Koh Hwa at No.65 Si Zung
Lee off Rue Brenier du Montmorand, French Concession.

I was married to my husband at Haimung in 1928 when
he was employed as a Sub-Inspector in the Haimung Police Bureau.
Four years after our marriage (1932) my husband was discharged
from his post for some unknown reason. He subsequently obtained
a position as an Inspector in the Kiangsu Water Police at
Tungchow. This job he kept for about three years and resigned
of his own accord. We then came to Shanghai and lived at our
present address. Since then my husband has not been successful
in obtaining employment and we had to live on the money remitted
to us from a bath-house in Haimung, of which my husband is a
part-owner.

I know nothing about my husband's political leanings
and I know very few of his friends. Yang Dien Wo (6th accused)
was introduced to my husband by one named Tsang Soong Liang,
a former superior officer of my husband. I am not on speaking
terms with Ting Zeu Daung although he resides next to me.
I am acquainted with Ting's wife because we usually met each
other in the alleyway.

以下为第十七被告赵熊氏（Zau Yoong Sz，趙熊氏）之陈述，
籍贯金堡（Kompo）。由本人副督察员科因（D.S.I. Coyne）
于1937年6月21日在杰斯菲尔德捕房总部（J.B., H.Q.）录取，并由副督察员施思坚（D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien）翻译

我叫赵熊氏（趙熊氏），29岁，籍贯金堡。我与丈夫赵国华（Zau Koh Hwa）居住在法租界蒙托邦路（Rue Brenier du Montmorand）芝宗里65号。

1928年，我在海门与丈夫结婚，当时他在海门警察局担任副巡官。婚后四年（1932年），丈夫因某种不明原因被免职。随后，他在通州获得了江苏水上警察督察员的职位。这份工作他做了大约三年，然后自愿辞职。之后我们来到上海，住在现在的地址。此后，丈夫一直未能成功找到工作，我们不得不依靠海门一家浴室汇来的钱生活，我丈夫是该浴室的部分所有者。

我对丈夫的政治倾向一无所知，也很少认识他的朋友。杨殿沃（第六被告）是由我丈夫的前上司张重良介绍给我丈夫的。虽然丁佐唐住在我隔壁，但我与他没有往来。我认识丁的妻子，因为我们通常在弄堂里见面。

Questioned regarding the origin of item 3 and 4 of List No.1 .
The information relating to the Water Police was supplied
by Tsang Soong Liang, Supt. of the 1st Division of the Kiangsu
Water Police, and a member of the Party, in March and April
1936. The information regarding other units was obtained by
Tsang and one named Ma Kyi (馬奇) also a member of the Water
Police, who has a large following in other services.
As Hu Han Min died shortly after the lists had been
compiled, I retained them and did not forward them to Liu
Loo Ying, as intended.
Questioned regarding List No.5.
Regarding the chit book bearing the chop "South Eastern
Retired Military Officers National Salvation Association,"
during Dec. 1931 I gathered together about ten persons and
It was my intention to organize a body bearing this title.
I applied for official recognition but was instructed by the
Shanghai Woosung Garrison Commander to cease my activities,
and the movement came to an end (Letter from Garrison Commander
on file).
The map showing the distribution of military units in
Kiangsu (item 29) was prepared by Tsang Soong Liang.
The booklet (item 32) containing anti-Japanese and anti-
Nanking sentiments issued by the Headquarters of the 67th Army
at Sian in January 1937 was given to me by one named Lee Yuen
Siau, now with the volunteers in the North (Notes issued at
the time of the Sian Incident.)
I do not know any of the more important members of the

Translation of one of the letters mentioned in Item No.24
of List No.I

Dear Pah Vung (柏文), Saung Dien (桑田), Kuo Hwa (國華),
Tsang Soong Liang (張重良); Pih Dah (必大) and Liu Wei
(劉匯),

Comrade Yang has arrived here. From him I know
that you are continuing in your efforts for the salvation of
the nation and are still faithful to the "ism," despite the
numerous hardships confronting you. I was very much
comforted by the news and indeed I greatly admire your
spirit.

Hereafter you should continue to follow the plan
which has been laid down and exert the most care to preserve
your energy so that you can make the best use of it when an
opportunity ripens.

I have talked to Yang what are to be attended to
for the time being and same will be conveyed to you by him.

Mei (眉)
31st Jan. (year not mentioned)

Translator's note:
Questioned regarding the letter, the 6th accused
Yang Dien We stated that Mei is an alias of Liu Im Ying and
the letter was written by Liu in January last year.
page_data.zh:
清单第I号第24项中提及的一封信件的译文

亲爱的柏文（Pah Vung）、桑田（Saung Dien）、国华（Kuo Hwa）、
张重良（Tsang Soong Liang）、必大（Pih Dah）和刘汇（Liu Wei），

杨同志已抵达此处。从他那里我得知
尽管面临诸多艰难困苦，你们仍在继续为拯救国家而努力，
并且仍然忠于“主义”。听到这个消息我感到非常欣慰，
确实非常钦佩你们的精神。

今后你们应继续遵循既定计划，并格外注意
保存精力，以便在时机成熟时能充分利用。

我已与杨交谈了目前需要注意的事项，
他将向你们转达。

眉（Mei）
1月31日（年份未注明）

译者注：
就该信件受询时，第六被告杨殿沃（Yang Dien We）称，“眉”是刘英（Liu Im Ying）的别名，
该信是刘于去年一月所写。

Translation of a draft of a report, including in item 24
of List No.I

I beg to report that an observation has been made
at various places with the following result being obtained:
The affairs in Changchow and Kiangyin are temporarily
controlled by Yee Tsung Wong (美通之) (a member of the
Young Military Men's Society). As I have friends in the
Kuomintang and officials organs of these two hsiens, efforts
are being made to establish connections with them.
The organization in Yangchow is handled by Zang Tien.
Yang Wei (楊蔚), commander of the 3rd Regiment of
Kiangsu Peace Preservation Corps, was formerly a subordinate
of mine. He is now arranging to establish connections between
the various units of Paoantui stationed in the various places
in Kiangpeh.
At Li-yang Hsien, the Chief of the Merchants' Volunteer
Corps, one named Loh, who is our comrade, is entrusted with
the task of establishing connections between volunteer corps
of various hsiens. There are in Li-yang a total of
10,000 rifles (? volunteer corps).
In Northern part of Anhwei, Yee Tsung Wong and Wu Mang
Tien (胡孟天) have succeeded in forming an organization of the
merchants volunteer corps, who are in possession of more
than 10,000 rifles.
You are requested to give them formal appointment so that
the work could be accelerated.
A number of pledge forms have been filled by members.
Names of those who have not filled the forms will be sent
to Shanghai by separate mail.

第一号清单第24项所附报告草稿译文

谨此报告，已在多处进行侦察，所得结果如下：
常州和江阴的事务目前由易宗旺（美通之）（青年军人学会成员）控制。因我在国民党及这两县的政府机关中有朋友，正努力与他们建立联系。
扬州的组织由臧天负责。
江苏保安团第三团团长杨蔚（楊蔚）曾是我的下属。他目前正在安排建立江北各地驻防的保安团各部队之间的联系。
在溧阳县，商团团长罗某是我们的同志，受托负责建立各县商团之间的联系。溧阳共有步枪10,000支（？属商团）。
在皖北，易宗旺和胡孟天（胡孟天）已成功组建商团组织，拥有步枪10,000余支。
请予他们正式委任，以便加速工作进展。
部分成员已填写誓约书。未填写者名单将另行邮寄至上海。

    From the statement made by Yang Dien Wo it appears

in the countries military organization and willing to sell his
services to any party able to offer him employment. He admits

Loo Ying. When questioned regarding persons in the pay of the

after its object had been explained to him by Yang Dien Wo. He
also admitted having given Ting Zeu Daung a pistol to dispose of
for him, but denied the allegation of Ting that he had also given
him a pistol from Yang.

(楊殿侯), My name is Yang Dien Wo (楊奠華) alias Yang Ting Hao
age 49 years. I was born at Kao Sung Hsien, Kiangsu
Province, where my father was a rice dealer.

I received my education from a private tutor between the
ages of six and fifteen, but my family being very poor, when I
was fifteen, as a result of conscription I went to Nanking and
there joined the army as a private soldier.

My services being satisfactory, at the age of eighteen I
was sent on a course for N.C.O.s and on passing out I attended
the Military Academy for six months, after which I became a cadet
officer.

At the outbreak of the Revolution in 1911 the army rose
against the Manchu regime and joined the revolutionaries; I was
appointed Company Commander and under General Pah Sung Wei (柏文蔚)
and fought against the Manchu Forces under General Chang Chun.
I was then 23 years of age.

During the revolution trained officers were permitted to
raise their own regiments and were appointed Regimental Commanders.
I therefore raise a regiment in Anhwei and I was appointed Com-
mander, being posted to the Shanghai Revolutionary Army and
stationed at the North Railway Station.

When my Regiment was disbanded several months later I
was successful in obtaining an appointment as staff officer with
the Governor of Kiangsu Province at Nanking. This appointment
only lasted a few months, so I went to Canton with a view to
obtaining employment in a military capacity, but meeting with
no success I returned to Nanking and became 2nd in command of

(楊殿侯)，我叫杨奠华（楊奠華），又名杨殿侯，
年龄49岁。我出生于江苏省高松县，父亲是一名米商。

六岁至十五岁期间，我跟随私塾老师接受教育，但因家境贫寒，十五岁时因征兵前往南京，
并在那里作为一名列兵入伍。

因表现良好，十八岁时我被送去参加士官课程，结业后进入军校学习六个月，之后成为见习军官。

1911年革命爆发时，军队反对满清政权并加入革命党；我被任命为连长，在柏文蔚（柏文蔚）将军麾下，
与张勋将军率领的满清军队作战。
当时我23岁。

革命期间，受过训练的军官被允许自行招募团级部队并被任命为团长。
因此，我在安徽招募了一个团，并被任命为团长，随后被派往上海革命军，
驻扎在北火车站。

几个月后我的团被解散，我成功在南京获得江苏省督军参谋一职。该职务
仅持续了几个月，于是我前往广州，试图谋求军事职位，但未获成功，我便返回南京，成为

When the army was reorganized I lost my post and for several
years was unemployed. I returned to my native place, but in
1917 I proceeded to Canton and there became A.D.C. to General
Zee Zau Tsung (徐紹楨), Garrison Commander. This office was
abolished when I had been there a few months and until 1919 I
was unemployed in Canton.
I came to Shanghai in 1919 and with another unemployed
man sent a letter to the Manager of the Sincere Co., Nanking
Road, demanding a sum of money for the relief of the comrades of
the Revolutionary Army. Whilst we were waiting in a teashop
to receive the money detectives arrived and arrested us, and found
a bomb which they alleged was ours, but which we believed had
been put there by the detectives seconds.
I was sentenced to four years imprisonment and on my
release in 1923 I went to Kaochow, Kwangtung Province, and there
吳川
obtained a post as acting magistrate of Wu Chuen Hsien, remain-
ing there for about one year.
(I forgot to mention that in 1917 the Cantonese Clique
subsidized an abortive rising in Shantung and I was appointed
Brigade Commander (without Brigade). The rebellion was suppressed
by the Peking Government).
After leaving Kaochow I went to Canton and General Chien
De Chuen (錢大鈞) (present Chief of General Staff) Commander
of the 20th Division appointed me Vice Commander of the Artillery
Company.

Party I was taken prisoner by the communist forces, but escaped
after a couple of weeks, and returned to my unit after which I
became A.D.C. to the Divisional Commander.
In 1928 I was appointed Chief of the Police Bureau of the
1st District of Ching Fu Hsien (青浦), remaining there for one year,
later being appointed Deputy Chief of the same force.
Resigning from the Police in 1931 I returned to the army
and was appointed Chief Adjutant of the Pacification Commission-
ers Office of Kiangse Province.
Early in 1932 one named Hsu Chi Jung (許紀云) the
Chairman of the Overseas Chinese Association gave me $500
travelling expenses and asked me to go to Jehol to investigate
the situation as he intended financing the volunteers.
I had many acquaintances then serving in the North and
with their assistance I raised a volunteer army which was known
as the 8th Route Anti-Japanese Army, and had several engagement
with the Manchukou troops. Hsu sent $1,000 towards the upkeep
of the army, and three or four thousand dollars were received
from other sources.
On the conclusion of the Tanku Truce in 1933 the army
under my command, then about 10,000 strong, was disbanded and
I returned to Shanghai.
On my way to Shanghai I passed through Kalgen and there
met one named Zau Siao Ching (曹小青) an agent of Mr. Hu Han
Ling. This person telegraphed to Hongkong telling Mr. Hu about
me, and a few days later I was instructed to go to Hongkong as
Mr. Hu wished to see me.

我曾被共产党军队俘虏，但数周后逃脱，并返回原部队，随后成为师长的副官（A.D.C.）。
1928年，我被任命为青浦县第一区警察局局长，在该职任职一年，后被任命为同一警队的副局长。
1931年我从警队辞职，重返军队，被任命为江西省绥靖公署主任参谋。
1932年初，一位名为许纪云（Hsu Chi Jung）的华侨协会主席给了我500美元旅费，并要求我前往热河调查局势，因为他打算资助义勇军。
当时我在北方有许多熟人，在他们的帮助下，我组建了一支志愿军，称为“第八路抗日军”，并与伪满洲国军队进行了数次交战。许寄来1,000美元作为军队维持费用，另从其他来源收到三四千美元。
1933年《塘沽协定》签订后，我所指挥的约一万人的军队被解散，我返回上海。
在前往上海的途中，我经过张家口（Kalgen），在那里遇到了一位名为曹小青（Zau Siao Ching）的人，他是胡汉龄（Hu Han Ling）先生的代理人。此人向香港发电报，将我的情况告知胡先生，几天后我接到指示前往香港，因为胡先生希望见我。

It was in April or May 1933 when I saw Mr. Hu Han Ming
苗高台
at his residence at Miao Kao Tai, Hongkong. After questioning
me closely regarding my antecedents and political views, he asked
me whether I was prepared to join the Koumintang of the South
West, the object of which was to unite all cliques and form
a united Anti-Japanese front. He said that unless this object
was achieved China would continue to suffer aggression at the
hands of Japan.
Then I stated that I fully agreed with the views expressed
by Mr. Hu suggested that, as I had a large circle of acquaintances in military and Police circles, I should organize a
following.
Persons found worthy of promotion would then be elected
to membership of the South West Koumintang. I undertook to
carry out the instructions of Mr. Hu and for my work I received
$200 per month from the South West Political Council, through
Mr. Liu Loo Ying, until December 1936.
Zeu Siao Ching, the person responsible for my introduction to Mr. Hu gave me my final instructions. He was the chief
of an organization known as the Young Military Men's Society of
the Kuomintang of China, and he told me that I would be responsible for the organizing of a branch in Kiangsu Province.
After a stay of several days in Hongkong I was instructed
by Mr. Hu Han Min to go to Canton and there see Mr. Liu Loo Ying,
as in future all my dealing would be with him.
Liu told me that the party was not satisfied with the
Nanking Government, and it was their intention to oppose the

那是1933年4月或5月，我在香港苗高台（Miao Kao Tai）胡汉明（Hu Han Ming）先生的寓所会见了他。在详细询问了我的身世和政治观点后，他问我是否准备加入西南国民党，其目的是团结各派系，组成统一的抗日阵线。他说，除非实现这一目标，否则中国将继续遭受日本的侵略。
随后我表示完全同意胡先生的观点，并建议鉴于我在军警界有广泛的熟人圈子，我应该组织一批追随者。
那些被认为值得提拔的人将被选为西南国民党的党员。我承诺执行胡先生的指示，为此工作，我通过刘鲁英（Liu Loo Ying）先生从西南政务委员会每月领取200美元，直至1936年12月。
负责将我引荐给胡先生的曹小青（Zeu Siao Ching）向我下达了最后指示。他是一个名为“中国国民党青年军人社”组织的负责人，他告诉我，我将负责在江苏省组建一个分部。
在香港停留数日后，胡汉民先生指示我前往广州，在那里会见刘鲁英先生，因为今后我的一切事务都将与他联系。

dictatorship set up by General Chiang Kai-shek. He gave me
final instructions regarding the method to be adopted in
organizing the Young Military Men's Society in Kiangsu and also
gave me a letter appointing me chief of the Young Military Men's
Society in this Province.
Returning to Shanghai, I set about my new duties, and
for three years travelled extensively recruiting members from
among military and police officials. The majority of the re-
cruits signed pledges to support the organization, and many of
these were forwarded to Mr. Hu Han Lin. Other recruits, because
of their high position, did not wish to risk signing the paper,
although they were prepared to assist in any way possible/ in
furthering the ends of the Party.
A number of the more important recruits did sign the
pledge form, which, because of their importance, were immediately
sent to Mr. Hu. Those in my possession are signed by persons of
secondary importance.
When Mr. Hu Han Min died in the summer of 1936 the
movement received a serious setback and for a time all activities
were suspended, but a few months later Mr. Liu Loo Ying instructed
that the movement be resumed as he has been appointed an member
of the Executive Committee Member of the South West Political
Council and intended supporting General Chen Chi Tang, who was
then preparing for open conflict with the Nanking Government.
After the death of Mr. Hu my salary did not arrive
regularly, and ceased altogether in December, 1936. Although I
received letters I did not receive any definite instructions so

回到上海后，我开始履行新职责，并在三年间广泛奔走，从军警官员中招募成员。大多数 recruits（新成员）签署了支持该组织的誓约，其中许多誓约被寄送给胡汉林（Hu Han Lin）先生。其他 recruits 由于地位较高，不愿冒险签署文件，尽管他们愿意以任何可能的方式协助推进党的目标。
一些较重要的 recruits 确实签署了誓约表，鉴于他们的重要性，这些誓约立即被送往胡先生处。我手中持有的誓约是由次要人物签署的。
1936年夏胡汉民先生去世时，该运动受到严重挫折，所有活动一度暂停，但几个月后，刘鲁英先生指示恢复运动，因为他已被任命为西南政务委员会执行委员会委员，并打算支持陈济棠将军，后者当时正准备与南京政府公开冲突。

when Mr. Loo came to Shanghai it was my intention to see him.
Before I could do so, however, he received a telegram from
the Central Government inviting him to attend the Plenary
Session of the Kuomintang then convened in Nanking.
On discovering that the Central Kuomintang did not
intend to adopt a stronger attitude vis-a-vis the Japanese
policy in China, he refused an invitation to see General Chiang
Kai-shek and at once returned to Shanghai. I called on him
at the Yangtsze Hotel, but as he was of the opinion that it
was not safe to discuss our business there, we decided to
meet later later elsewhere. Before I could get into touch
with him again he was arrested. He had realized whilst in
Nanking that he was in danger of being arrested in connection
with the Yang Yung Tai case and it was for that reason that
he returned to Shanghai, where he thought he would be safe.
Being without income it was my intention to go to Nanking
or Kwangse in search of employment. I do not know Ting □□
(4th accused) and I did not sent a pistol to him.
I know Zau Koh Hwa (趙國華) as he became a member of
my organization over a year ago, being introduced by Tsang Zung
Liang (張重良) a former military friend of mine.

（印：POLICE BRANCH / 22 JUNE 1937 / SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

当刘（Loo）来到上海时，我本打算去见他。
然而，在我这样做之前，他收到了中央政府邀请他参加当时在南京召开的国民党全体会议的电报。
在发现中央国民党不打算对中国境内的日本政策采取更强硬的态度后，他拒绝了会见蒋介石将军的邀请，并立即返回上海。我去扬子饭店拜访了他，但由于他认为在那里讨论我们的事务不安全，我们决定稍后在其他地方见面。在我再次与他取得联系之前，他被捕了。他在南京时已意识到自己因杨永泰案而有被捕的危险，正因如此他才返回上海，他认为在那里会是安全的。
由于没有收入，我本打算去南京或广西寻找工作。我不认识丁□□（第四被告），我也没有向他发送手枪。
我认识赵国华（Zau Koh Hwa），因为他在一年多前成为我组织的成员，是由我以前的军中朋友张重良（Tsang Zung Liang）介绍的。

My name is Zau Koh Hwa (趙國華) alias Zau Pah Tsoo
(趙柏初) alias Zau Lo (趙錄), native of Ziang Fu Hsien
(祥符), Honan Province where I was born in 1897. My
father was a Chinese style boxing instructor,

I had no education and when I was 15 years old I
joined the army at Soochow. When 17 years old I became a
policeman in the Kiangsu Water Police and was promoted sergeant,
but in 1925, owing to a change of Commissioner I lost my
position.

In 1926 I was successful in obtaining an appointment
as sergeant of the Haimun Police and was later promoted Sub-
Inspector, but with the change of administration in 1929 I
again lost my job.

In 1930 I obtained a position as Sub-Inspector in the
18th Division of the Kiangsu River Police at Tungchow. The
following year I resigned and returned to Haimun, where I
invested $1,250 in a bath-house. The Chief of Police, who was
a friend of mine, appointed me honorary Chief Detective, with
a monthly allowance of $20.

In 1933 I came to Shanghai in search of employment but
was unable to obtain a position.

In June 1936 one named Tsang Soong Liang, a former
comrade in the Water Police, offered to introduce me to Yang
Dien Wo (楊殿華), an influential person who might be able
to obtain an appointment for me in some Police force. He took
me to the Sing Liu Sao Hotel (新旅社), Kiukiang Road, where
I met Yang, who promised to try to get a job for me. Two weeks

以下为第十六被告赵国华（Zau Koh Hwa），又名赵柏初（Zau Pah Tsoo），又名赵录（Zau Lo）之陈述。
籍贯河南，由本人 D.S.I. Coyne
于1937年6月18日在中央捕房总部（C.B.,H.Q.）录取，并由 D.S.I. Shih 翻译。

我叫赵国华（Zau Koh Hwa），又名赵柏初（Zau Pah Tsoo），又名赵录（Zau Lo），籍贯河南省祥符县（Ziang Fu Hsien），1897年出生于该地。我的父亲是一位中式拳术教练，

我没有受过教育，15岁时在苏州参军。17岁时，我成为江苏水上警察的一名警察，并晋升为警长，但在1925年，由于局长更替，我失去了职位。

1926年，我成功获得海门警察局警长的任命，后来晋升为巡官，但随着1929年行政当局更迭，我再次失业。

1930年，我在通州获得了江苏江防第十八师巡官的职位。次年我辞职回到海门，投资1,250美元开设了一家浴室。警察局长是我的朋友，任命我为荣誉首席侦探，每月津贴20美元。

1933年，我来上海寻找工作，但未能获得职位。

1936年6月，一位名叫张松良（Tsang Soong Liang）的前水上警察同事提出将我介绍给杨殿华（Yang Dien Wo），这是一位有影响力的人物，或许能帮我在某支警察部队中获得任命。他带我到九江路的新旅社（Sing Liu Sao Hotel），在那里我见到了杨，他答应尽力为我找工作。两周

later I again called on Yang at the Chang Chun Hotel (長春),
Hotel Chekiang Road, and he then explained to me that he was
the Shanghai Chief of the Young Military Men's Party of the
Kuomintang Party of China, and after telling me about it, and
what it stood for, he asked me to become a member.
When I agreed to his suggestion he told me that I
would receive $10 or $20 each month until Mr. Hu Han Ming came
into power, when I would be appointed to some post.
I agree that I signed a pledge to support the Young
Military Men's Society and that in the pledge it was stated that
the object of the Party was to overthrow the Dictator, and the
Dictator referred to was General Chiang Kai-shek.
I saw Yang Dien Wo several times in the Chang Chun
Hotel, Chekiang Road, and there was introduced by Yang to the
following persons:
Lieu Chi Wei (劉既偉), Ex-Sub Inspector of the Kiangsu
Water Police at Lieu Ho (瀏河);
Zang Tien (田), Ex Sub-Inspector of the Soochow
Police;
Tsu Han Ching (朱漢卿), a close firend of Zang Tien.
Although I knew that these men were members of the
Party I never heard business discussion by them with Yang.
On one of the visits Yang told me that although Mr.
Hu Han Min was the head of the organization, due to pressure
of business it was his practice to leave the management of
affairs to Liu Loo Ying, Chief of the Propaganda Department of
the Central Government.

后，我再次在浙江路的长春酒店（Chang Chun Hotel）拜访杨，他当时向我解释，他是中国国民党青年军人党的上海负责人，在向我介绍了该党及其宗旨后，他邀请我加入。
当我同意他的建议时，他告诉我，在胡汉明先生掌权之前，我每月将收到10或20美元，届时我将被任命某个职位。
我承认我签署了一份支持“青年军人社”的誓约，并且誓约中声明该党的目标是推翻独裁者，所指独裁者即蒋介石将军。
我在浙江路的长春酒店多次见到杨殿华，并在那里经杨介绍认识了以下人员：
刘既伟（Lieu Chi Wei），前浏河（Lieu Ho）江苏水上警察巡官；
田（Zang Tien），前苏州警察巡官；
朱汉卿（Tsu Han Ching），田的密友。
虽然我知道这些人是该党成员，但我从未听到他们与杨讨论事务。
在一次拜访中，杨告诉我，虽然胡汉民先生是该组织的领袖，但由于公务繁忙，他的惯例是将事务管理交给中央政府宣传部长刘鲁英（Liu Loo Ying）。

Although Yang had promised us money we had received none, therefore, fearing that Zang Tien would press him when the news of the arrest of Liu Loo Ying appeared in the papers, Yang removed from Rue Paul Beu, and we were unable to find him.
About two months ago X Zang Tien gave me a pistol which he had brought from the Soochow Police and asked me to sell it for him for $20. I gave it to Ting (4th accused) with instruction to sell it for $30. but after that I did not see him again and I suspected that he had absconded with the pistol.
The handbills bearing circular telegrams issued by the South Western Political Council denouncing the tyranical policy of General Chiang Kai-shek, which were found in my home, were given to me by Yang Dien Wo 10 days after I had joined his party He also instructed me to distribute the handbills among my friends.

虽然杨氏曾许诺给我们钱款，但我们分文未收。因此，因担心刘罗英（Liu Loo Ying，音译）被捕的消息见报后，臧天（Zang Tien，音译）会向杨氏施压，杨氏便从保罗·伯路（Rue Paul Beu，即今重庆南路）搬离，致使我们无法找到他。

约两个月前，臧天交给我一支他从苏州警察局带来的手枪，让我以20美元的价格代为出售。我将该枪交给丁某（第四名被告），指示其以30美元的价格出售。但此后我便再未见过他，我怀疑他已携枪潜逃。

在我家中搜出的印有西南政务委员会谴责蒋介石将军暴政之通电传单的传单，是我加入该党十天后由杨殿沃（Yang Dien Wo，音译）交给我的。他还指示我在朋友中分发这些传单。

He states: The note on a piece of letter paper of the Fah

year, asking me to go to the Ping Shiang Tea Shop at the corner

On the following day I met Lieu Chi Wei at his home, (at the

had left a note in my home and that he wished to introduced to
me one of his friends named Tung (董), a clerk of an
opium shop in Nantao.

The Fah Sung News agency was organized in 1935 by Wong Yu

Dah Kung Newspaper in Haimung. I February 1936 he sold the
business to some other persons because his paper had a very

became the manager of the An Saung Lodging House (behind the
Great World Amusement Resort). Wong and his wife removed from
the lodging house to stay together with me at No.64 Zee Zung Li,
Rue Brenier de Montmorend in January, 1937. In February he left

以下为丁祖堂（Ting Zeu Daung，音译）之补充供词（第二次）……
籍贯……由本人……于1937年6月18日在……讯问，并由……翻译。

注：就清单第4号第6项（在其家中搜获之物产）对丁祖堂进行讯问，该项为一张写在纸片上的便条，内容与第4项类似，写道：“下午4时至5时，在拉斐特路（Rue Lafayette，即今复兴中路）与马尔谢路（Rue Marche，即今淡水路）拐角处的品香茶楼。”

他陈述道：这张写在法声通讯社信纸上的便条是由崔既卫（Lieu Chi Wei）所写，此人我在之前的供词中曾提及。时间是今年四月某时，他约我去拉斐特路与马尔谢路拐角处的品香茶楼。那天我回家时并未看到这张纸条，所以我没有去茶楼。次日，我在他家（位于拉斐特路与拉比兹路（Rue Rabiez，即今建国中路）拐角处）见到了崔既卫。他告诉我他曾在我家留了一张便条，并希望能向我介绍他的一位姓董的朋友，此人是南市一家鸦片店的职员。

法声通讯社由黄玉清（Wong Yu Ching，音译）于1935年组建。我于1935年10月在海门结识黄某，当时我在海门禁烟督察公署担任侦探。黄某当时在海门经营《大公报》。1936年2月，因报纸发行量极小，他将生意转卖给他人。1936年8月，他来到上海，成为安松旅馆（位于大世界游乐场后方）的经理。1937年1月，黄某及其妻子从旅馆搬出，与我一同居住在蒙莫朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand，即今建国东路）济宗里64号。2月他离开

CONFIDENTIAL

REPORT

Subject Documents seized at the home of Yang Dien Wo (楊英華)
and a statement made by Ting Zau Daung. 丁聚堂 )

Made by D.S.I. Coyne. Forwarded by

Forwarded herewith is a tabulated list of a number of
documents siezed by the Municipal Police at the Home of one
Yang Dien Wo (楊英華 ) 260. Rue Lafayette, French Concession,
on June 16, 1937.

Yang was arrested on June 14, and together with twelve
other persons was ordered by the Shanghai First Special District
Court the following day to be detained in the custody of the
Municipal Police pending an investigation into their believed
criminal activities.

An examination of the documents revealed that Yang was
for many years a military officer and in 1930 was employed in
Kiangsi as Chief Adjutant of the Pacification Commanders Head-
quarters. A card bearing his name and describing him as the
"Commander of the 8th Route Anti-Japanese Army in Jehol" was
also found. Lists relating to the disposition, strenght and
arms of various military, Police, Water Police and volunteer
units in Kiangsu Province, together with maps, indicated the
careful collection of data by what would appear to be a large
organization.

The most important item of the seizure is probably a
letter signed by Liu Loo Ying in which it is stated that
Comrade Yang Dien Wo (楊英華) is appointed Chief of the Kiangsu
Joint Office of the Councillors Group.

A bundle of about 120 papers on examination proved to be
the enrollment forms of persons who had sworn to support the
Young Military Men's Society of the Kuomintang Party of China.
In addition to stating their antecedents the recruits to the
Party had also been required to state their political views.
The majority of these were "Anti-Japanese", "Anti-Imperialist"

报告

主题：在杨英华（Yang Dien Wo）家中搜获的文件及丁聚堂（Ting Zau Daung）的供词。

由副督察长科因（D.S.I. Coyne）呈报。转呈人

随函附上表格一份，列明1937年6月16日公共租界警务处在法租界拉斐特路（Rue Lafayette）260号杨英华（楊英華）家中搜获的若干文件。

杨于6月14日被捕，次日，上海第一特区地方法院下令将其与另外十二人一并羁押于公共租界警务处看管，以待对其涉嫌犯罪活动进行调查。

经检查这些文件发现，杨多年来是一名军官，1930年在江西任职，担任绥靖公署总部 chief adjutant（首席副官/主任参谋）。还发现一张印有他名字的名片，称其为“热河抗日第八路军司令”。有关江苏省各军事、警察、水警及志愿团体的部署、兵力和武装情况的清单，以及地图，表明似乎有一个大型组织在仔细收集情报。

此次搜获物品中最重要的可能是一封由刘蘅隐（Liu Loo Ying）签名的信件，信中声明任命杨英华同志（楊英華）为江苏参事团联合办事处主任。

经查，一捆约120份文件系宣誓支持中国国民党青年军人社的人员登记表。除陈述个人履历外，入党者还被要求陈述其政治观点。其中大多数为“抗日”、“反帝”

"Anti-Fascist" "Reform the Party to Resist outside Aggression"
When briefly questioned Yang stated that he was the agent
of Liu Loo Ying and responsible for the activities and
organization of the Young Military Men's Party in Kiangsu.
When more is known about the other persons in custody a
statement will be taken from Yang.

The second subject of this report is the state-
ment made Ting Zeu Daung (丁野堂) who was arrested at the
Sing San Klang Lodging House, 495. Canton Rd together with Wong
Kyah Kyi (王介共), a pistol being found in the room
occupied by them.

Regarding that part on the statement bearing
on political matters, from events which have occurred since
the time he became a member of the organization headed locally
by Yang, there is no reason to doubt the veracity of his story.
It is well known that Liu Loo Ying was convicted at Hankow
for heading an anti-Government clique moreso than for complicity
in the murder of Yang Yung Tai.

That part of his statement concerning the turning
to criminal activities owing to lack of funds from the party
may equally be believed. The story is not new to the Police for
it was under the same circumstances that a number of men
belonging the communist assassination squads were eventually
arrested.

Efforts are now being made to ascertain whether any of
the arrested persons served with Hwa Kuh Ta or knew him or
other members of the assassination squad which worked in
Shanghai on behalf of the South-Eastern Clique.

Shaw
D.S.I.

“反法西斯”、“改组政党以抵抗外来侵略”
杨在接受简短讯问时声称，他是刘蘅隐的代理人，负责江苏青年军人党的活动和组织工作。待对其他在押人员有更多了解后，将再取杨的供词。

本报告的第二项内容是丁野堂（Ting Zeu Daung，译注：此处原文拼音与后文供词中的丁聚堂/Ting Zau Daung 略有差异，但根据上下文及后文供词，应指同一人或关联紧密者，此处依原文拼音译为丁野堂，括号内保留原中文名丁聚堂以供参照，或依后文统一为丁聚堂，鉴于后文明确写出丁聚堂，此处暂按音译并备注）的供词，他与王介共（Wong Kyah Kyi）一同在广东路495号新三康旅馆（Sing San Klang Lodging House）被捕，在他们居住的房间内发现了一支手枪。

关于其供词中涉及政治事项的部分，鉴于自他加入由杨在当地领导的组织以来所发生的事件，没有理由怀疑其陈述的真实性。众所周知，刘蘅隐在汉口被判刑，更多是因为领导反政府派系，而非因参与谋杀杨永泰。

至于其供词中关于因缺乏党派资金而转向犯罪活动的部分，同样可信。这种情况对警方来说并不新鲜，因为此前多名属于共产党暗杀队的成员也是在相同情况下最终被捕的。

目前正努力查明被捕人员中是否有任何人曾为华固达（Hwa Kuh Ta，音译）效力，或认识他或其他代表东南派系在上海活动的暗杀队成员。

肖（Shaw）
副督察长

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Ting Zeu Daung (丁聚堂) Ting Zang Piau 丁長標
native of Hwei Wing, Kompo taken by me D.S.I.Coyne
at on the Lune 16, 1937 and interpreted by D.S.I.Shih.

My name is Ting Zeu Daung (丁聚堂) alias Ting Zang
Piau (丁長標) and at the time of my arrest I resided
at 64. Zee Zung Li, Route Brenier de Montmorand, French
Concession.
My father, Ting Chi Yee (丁奇義) was a farmer owning
land at Hwei Ying, Kompo, where I was born in 1901.
My parents died whilst I was still a child and I was
brought up by my uncle, 丁奇寅 Ting Chi Bing, who did about
six years ago.
I received no education, and until I was 19 years
old I worked on the family farm. Owing to poverty I
went to Nanking seeking employment and eventually joined
the army and served with the 4th Mixed Brigade of the
forces of General Chi Shueh Yuan (齊燮元) then Governor
of Kiangsu Province.
The following year, 1920, I was taken prisoner in the
civil war between General Chi and Sung Chuan Fang, the
Chekiang warlord, and thereafter became an N.C.O. in the
14th Battalion of the 4th Division of the latters forces.
In 1926 when Sung Chuan Fang's forces were defeated by
the Nationalist Army I was taken prisoner and became an
N.C.O. in the 2nd Independant Battalion under General
姚安
Chen Tiau Yuen at Yau An, Kompo.
In 1927 I left the army and lived for one year at
Chingkiang, but being unable to obtain employment I went
to Nan-tung and became an assistant in a cigarette shop
owner by a former comrade named Yen Sih Woo (閻錫武)
remaining with him until 1931.

以下为丁聚堂（Ting Zeu Daung），又名丁长标（Ting Zang Piau），广东惠阳籍人，于1937年6月16日由我，副督察长科因，在______录取，并由副督察长石（Shih）翻译的供词。

我叫丁聚堂（Ting Zeu Daung），别名丁长标（Ting Zang Piau），被捕时居住在法租界蒙马兰路（Route Brenier de Montmorand）西成里64号。
我的父亲丁奇义（Ting Chi Yee）是广东惠阳的一名农民，拥有土地，我于1901年出生在那里。
我在孩童时期父母双亡，由叔父丁奇寅（Ting Chi Bing，原文汉字为丁奇寅，拼音为Ting Chi Bing）抚养长大，他于大约六年前去世。
我没有受过教育，直到19岁都在家庭农场劳作。由于贫困，我去南京谋职，最终参军，在时任江苏省督军齐燮元（Chi Shueh Yuan）将军部队的第四混成旅服役。
次年，即1920年，我在齐燮元与浙江军阀孙传芳（Sung Chuan Fang）之间的内战中被俘，此后成为孙传芳部队第四师第十四营的一名士官。
1926年，当孙传芳的部队被国民革命军击败时，我被俘，并在安徽姚安（Yau An, Kompo，译注：Kompo通常指广东，但此处语境似指安徽某地，或为OCR错误，姚安在云南，但结合陈调元防区，可能指安徽某地，此处保留原文地名逻辑，若姚安为云南则与陈调元防区不符，暂按原文音译处理，或疑为“姚安”即安徽某地之误写，但依规则不脑补，故保留姚安）陈调元（Chen Tiau Yuen）将军麾下的第二独立营担任士官。
1927年我离开军队，在镇江生活了一年，但因找不到工作，我去了南通，在一家由前战友阎锡武（Yen Sih Woo）拥有的香烟店当助手，一直留在他那里直到1931年。

Through the influence of a friend named Ching
Kwen San (秦昆山), Chief of the Special Affairs Section
of the Magistrates Office, I obtained employment with
the Opium Suppression Bureau at Nantung (南通) as a detective of
at $14 per month. When the Bureau was abolished in May
1933 I returned to Chingkiang and sought my friend Cheng
Kwen San to ask him to assist me to find work, he then
being Chief of Chingkiang Water Police. I did not get a
job and in November 1933, Ching alleged that I owed him
$400 and when I denied this he falsely accused me of
trafficking in arms, producing two pistols found in a hotel.
I was sent to Nantung for trial and in August 1934 was
convicted on charges of being the leader of a criminal
gang and possession of arr. and sentenced to life
imprisonment. In March 1936 my appeal to the Kiangsu
High Court, Soochow, was successful and I was pronounced
"not guilty," and released.

Following my release I went to Nantung and there
saw Tung Wei Pah (董会柏), the Chief Detective of the
Opium Suppression Bureau, who was formerly employed in the
Salt Gabelle. Tung gave me employment as a detective in
the Hai-mung (海门) branch of the Opium Suppression Bureau and
also supplied me with a pistol, although it was not
compulsory for detectives to own pistols. After following
this employment for three months without drawing any
salary, I resigned, returned the pistol to Tung Wei Pah,
and came to Shanghai. I went to live with Zau Koh

通过一位名叫秦昆山（Ching Kwen San）的朋友的影响，他是法院书记室特别事务科科长，我在南通禁烟局获得了一份侦探的工作，月薪14美元。当该局于1933年5月撤销时，我回到镇江，去找我的朋友秦昆山，请他帮我找工作，他当时是镇江水警科长。我没有找到工作，1933年11月，秦声称我欠他400美元，当我否认时，他诬告我贩卖军火，并出示了在一家旅馆发现的两支手枪。我被送往南通受审，并于1934年8月因领导犯罪团伙和持有武器罪被判终身监禁。1936年3月，我向苏州江苏高等法院提出的上诉成功，我被宣判“无罪”并获释。

获释后，我去了南通，在那里见到了董会柏（Tung Wei Pah），他是禁烟局的总侦探，以前曾在盐务稽核所工作。董雇佣我在禁烟局海门（Hai-mung）分局担任侦探，并提供给我一支手枪，尽管侦探并不强制拥有手枪。在这份工作上干了三个月却没有领到薪水后，我辞职了，把手枪还给了董会柏，然后来到上海。我去和赵国华（Zau Koh Hwa）同住

Hwa (赵国华), formerly an inspector attached to the Nantung
Water Police, who owns a bathhouse at Nantung but resides at
at 65 Zee Zong Lee (西成里), Rue Montmorand, French Concession.
Before resigning I had written to Zau asking him
whether he could find me employment in Shanghai and he had
replied in the affirmative.
On my arrival he told me that before his death, Mr. Hu
Han Ming had wished to overthrow the Nanking Government and
to this end had organized a secret party. The reason for
this was that Mr. Hu advocated resistance of Japanese aggression,
whilst the Nanking Government did not.
Zau went on to explain that the party was controlled
by Liu Loo Ying (刘蘅隐) who had been a close follower of
Mr. Hu and that the party programme remained the same.
It was as a member of this party that I was to have
employment, Zau telling me that he would introduce me to the
agent of Liu Loo Ying.
The following day I was taken by Zau to the Yangtsze
Hotel and in a room on the third floor was introduced to Yang
Dien Wu (杨典章) (6th accused) and Lieu Chi Wei (刘既会)
(not arrested, a follower of Yang).
After questioning me briefly regarding my past,
Yang repeated the statement of Zau as to the policy of Liu Loo
Ying, and stated that he was in charge of the activities of
the secret organization in Kiangsu Province. He then went
on to explain that the organization was determined to fight
the Japanese, if the Nanking Government agreed, so much the

赵国华（Zau Koh Hwa），他以前是南通水警的一名巡官，在南通拥有一家浴室，但居住在法租界蒙马兰路西成里65号。
在辞职之前，我曾写信给赵，问他能否在上海为我找到工作，他回信表示可以。
我到达后，他告诉我，胡汉民先生在去世前希望推翻南京政府，并为此组织了一个秘密政党。原因是胡先生主张抵抗日本侵略，而南京政府则不主张。
赵接着解释说，该党由刘蘅隐（Liu Loo Ying）控制，刘曾是胡先生的亲信追随者，且该党的纲领保持不变。
我将作为该党成员获得工作，赵告诉我他会把我介绍给刘蘅隐的代理人。
第二天，赵带我去了扬子饭店，在三楼的一个房间里，把我介绍给了杨典章（Yang Dien Wu，译注：此处拼音与首页杨英华/Yang Dien Wo不同，但标注为第六被告，可能为同一人或笔误，依原文拼音译为杨典章）（第六被告）和刘既会（Lieu Chi Wei）（未被捕，杨的追随者）。
在简要询问了我的过去后，杨重复了赵关于刘蘅隐政策的说法，并声称他负责江苏省秘密组织的活动。他接着解释说，该组织决心抗击日本，如果南京政府同意，那再好不过；

The overthrow would be brought about when the Kiangsi troops
under Generals Pai Tsoong Shi and Li Tsoong Jen advanced on
Kiangsu Province, for their way would be prepared by members
of the organization, who, by the use of anti-Japanese propaganda,
would stir up the people.
My section chief would be Zau Koh Hwa (趙國華)
and it would be my duty when the revolution got under way, and
the Kiangsi troops had reached Anhwei Province, to go to
Nantung and Hai-mung and by means of propganda prepare the
Magistrates and Police officials for the impending change in
regime.
My salary would for the time being be $15 per month,
and I was to do nothing but keep myself in readiness. I did
not receive any money but was told that as soon as he (Yang)
received something from Liu, I would be paid. Yang also told
me that in future I would receive instructions from Zau.
I resided with Zau for two days and then rented a
room in the next house, bringing my wife to live with me after
a couple of months.
No money being forthcoming I asked Zau when I was
likely to receive some, but he kept putting me off with the
explanation that Liu Loo Ying was in Hongkong and the money
could not be obtained. When Liu went to Nanking Zau told
me that we would be paid when he returned to Shanghai, but he
was arrested and I got nothing. I was so poor that for the
past six months I have not paid for my room, I had to borrow

List of Literature, documents, etc. seized at No. 260
Rue Lafayette on 16/6/37
---

1. A letter of appointment which reads as follows:-

"Comrade Yang Dien Wo is hereby appointed Chief
of the Kiangsu Joint Office of the Councilors
Group"
(Signed) Liu Lu Ying (刘蘆英).
April 1."

2. Two cards bearing the biography of Yang Ting Hou, an
alias of Yang Dien Wo. The following is a translation
of Yang's biography:-
"Yang Ting Hou, age 45, native of Kao Zung, Kiangsu,
is a graduate of Artillery Course of the Nanyang
Military Academy. After graduation (in Ching Dynasty)
served as a company commander in the army.
In the beginning of the 1912 Commander of the 3rd
Regiment of the 3rd Anti-Yuan (Yuan Shih Kai) Army.
1918 Commander of the 2nd Brigade of the 15th Joint
Army of the Kiangsu, Shantung, Honan and Anhwei
Provinces. 1924 Magistrate of the Wu Chuan Hsien,
Kwangtung Province, and concurrently commander of
the Guerilla Warfare Group of the Hsien. 1926
Commander of the Artillery Company of the 20th
Division of the Revolutionary Army. 1927 Chief
of the 1st Branch of the Bureau of Public Safety
of Chingpu Hsien, Kiangsu; resigned from the post
in 1928. 1929 re-assumed the post. 1930 retired
from the job owing to sickness. July 1930 appointed
Chief of the Adjutants Office of the Kiangsi Province
Pacification Commander's Headquarters."

3. Lists showing strength of Paotui, Police, River Police,
and merchants volunteer corps stationed in Kiangyin (江陰),
Fenghsien (奉賢), Sungkiang (松江), Kiangsu Province,
as well as lists showing the number and quality of munitions
and guns used by the Kiangsu River Police. These lists
were compiled in March and April 1936. (12 pages)

4. Lists showing connections between the Society (the Young
Military Men's Society of the Kuomintang Party of China)
and the Paotui, Merchants' Volunteer Corps and River

四月一日。”

2. 两张载有杨典华别名杨廷侯生平简历的卡片。以下是杨氏简历的译文：-
“杨廷侯，45岁，江苏高宗（音译）人，南洋陆军学堂炮兵科毕业。毕业后（清朝时期）在军中担任连长。
1912年初，任反袁（袁世凯）军第三军第三团团长。
1918年，任苏鲁豫皖四省联军第十五军第二旅旅长。1924年，任广东省吴川县县长，兼该县游击队司令。1926年，任革命军第二十师炮兵连连长。1927年，任江苏青浦县公安局第一分局局长；1928年辞职。1929年复职。1930年因病离职。1930年7月，被任命为江西省绥靖公署副官处处长。”

3. 列明驻扎在江苏省江阴、奉贤、松江等地的保卫团、警察、水警及商团志愿队实力的清单，以及列明江苏省水警所用弹药和枪支数量及质量的清单。这些清单编制于1936年3月和4月。（共12页）

4. 列明该会社（中国国民党青年军人社）与江苏省保卫团、商团志愿队及水警之间联系的清单。在这些清单中提及以下项目：-（共4页）

“地点名称（县）。

备注。”

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

ARREST OF A CRIMINAL GANG AND
SEIZURE OF ARMS & AMMUNITION.

At about 9 a.m. June 14th. 1937, detectives attached to C.I. acting on information received by D.I. Liu Zau Kwei and C.D.S. 304, raided Room No.7 of the "Dah Ming" (大鳴) Lodging House, No. 84, Thibet Road, and took into custody the two under - mentioned persons : -

1) WONG AH NYI (王阿二), aged 39 years, native of Yangchow, M/Unemployed, Country house off Poo Zau Road (普喜路), Chapei;

2) KWOH SIAU SAN TS (郭小三子), aged 21 years, native of Kempo, S/Coolie, No.6 Fun Tsung Li (豐潤里), Ching Kang Road (京江路), Chapei.

A search of the room revealed one 6.35 "UNION" Automatic Pistol, No.4345, one magazine containing nine rounds of ammunition and one .32 Spanish make Automatic pistol, No.12620, complete with one magazine and six rounds of ammunition, hidden under a bed pillow.

The two arrested men were conveyed to this office, where on being questioned, they admitted having committed armed robberies within the International Settlement.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The Political significance of this case as it actually is was revealed during the evening of the 15th June 1937 when the arrested persons were interrogated. The gang is apparently divided up into two sections under the leadership of the 6th accused Yang Dien Wo (杨英华). This man admitted that he was formerly a follower of the late Dr. Hu Han Min (胡汉民), one of the Canton Political leaders. On the death of Dr. Hu Han Min, the leadership of this particular party devolved upon the person of Mr. Lieu In Ying (刘静), who is at present serving a term of imprisonment for being concerned in the murder of the late General Yang Yeong Tai (杨永泰), formerly Governor General of the Hopei Province. It seems that Lieu's party is definitely determined by making use of the existing Anti-Japanese sentiment to undermine the prestige of the Central Government. For this purpose Lieu had appointed numerous agents to carry on propaganda with a view to the enlistment of as many members as possible. The 6th accused was appointed personally by Mr. Lieu In Ying as his chief agent for the Province of Kiangsu. Following the imprisonment of Mr. Lieu In Ying the party experienced great difficulty in raising sufficient funds to enable them to carry out their activities. 本案实际具有的政治意义在1937年6月15日晚审讯被捕人员时得以揭示。该团伙显然在第六被告杨英华（Yang Dien Wo）的领导下分为两部分。此人承认他曾是广东政治领袖之一、已故胡汉民博士的追随者。胡汉民博士去世后，该特定派系的领导权落到了刘静（Lieu In Ying）先生身上，此人目前正因参与谋杀前河北省主席杨永泰将军一案服刑。看来，刘氏一派决意利用现有的反日情绪来削弱中央政府的威望。为此，刘氏任命了许多代理人进行宣传，旨在招募尽可能多的成员。第六被告由刘静先生亲自任命为其江苏省首席代理人。在刘静先生入狱后，该派系在筹集足够资金以维持活动方面遇到了极大困难。随后策划了一个方案，通过

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The Political significance of this case as it actually is was revealed during the evening of the 15th June 1937 when the arrested persons were interrogated. The gang is apparently divided up into two sections under the leadership of the 6th accused Yang Dien Wo (楊奠華). This man admitted that he was formerly a follower of the late Dr. Hu Han Min (胡漢民), one of the Canton Political leaders. On the death of Dr. Hu Han Min, the leadership of this particular party devolved upon the person of Mr. Lieu La Ying (劉蘆隱), who is at present serving a term of imprisonment for being concerned in the murder of the late General Yang Yoong Tai (楊永泰), formerly Governor General of the Hopei Province. It seems that Lieu's party is definitely determined by making use of the existing Anti-Japanese sentiment to undermine the prestige of the Central Government. For this purpose Lieu had appointed numerous agents to carry on propaganda with a view to the enlistment of as many members as possible. The 6th accused was appointed personally by Mr. Lieu La Ying as his chief agent for the Province of Kiangsu. Following the imprisonment of Mr. Lieu La Ying the party experienced great difficulty in raising sufficient funds to enable them to carry out their activities. A scheme was then evolved to raise the necessary funds by

本案实际的政治意义在1937年6月15日晚对被逮捕人员的审讯中显露出来。该团伙显然在第六名被告杨奠华的领导下分为两个部分。此人承认他曾是已故胡汉民博士的追随者，胡是广东政治领袖之一。胡汉民博士去世后，这一特定派系的领导权落到了刘芦隐先生身上，刘目前正因参与谋杀前河北省总督杨永泰将军一案服刑。看来，刘的派系决心利用现有的反日情绪来破坏中央政府的威望。为此，刘任命了许多代理人进行宣传，旨在招募尽可能多的成员。第六名被告由刘芦隐先生亲自任命为其江苏省首席代理人。刘芦隐先生入狱后，该派系在筹集足够资金以开展活动方面遇到了极大困难。于是策划了一个方案，通过

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
As the result of a telephone message circulated to all Divisions, identification parades were held at Louza Station at 2:30 p.m. June 17th. 1937, but not one of the prisoners, paraded before the complainants was identified.
The 16th. 17th. 18th. 19th. and 20th. accused persons appeared before the 1st. S.S.D.C. during the morning of the 18th. June, 1937, when the "Writ of Detention" applied for was granted and they were ordered to be detained in custody until the 22nd. June, 1937.
A further report on the political aspect of this case was forwarded by D.S.I. Coyne on the 18th. June, 1937. Attached to this report were statements made by the 4th. 6th. and 16th. accused concerning their political activities, and lists of documents and other matter seized from the 4th. and 16th. accused, and from the home of one named Van Ming, who is still being sought in connection with this case.
The facts relating to the political activities of this gang were revealed to General Yang Hu, Commander of the local Garrison by C.D.I. Prince and Supt. Loh Li Kwei during the morning of the 18th. June, 1937.
Certain documents substantiating the information given were shown to the General, who requested a loan of same until the following Monday. These documents were handed over to General Yang Hu, who returned them into the

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

No.84, Fight Road, in possession of one 6.35 "U.P." Auto Pistol, No. 4365, out of nine rounds of ammunition and one .38 Spanish make Auto Pistol, No.12820, with six rounds of ammunition. These two pistols they stated were given to them by one not in custody known to them as Dah Fah To (火子). A brass knuckled pistol was also found at the home of the last accused.

4th, 5th, and 16th accused - Possession of Arms and Trafficking in Arms ( House 2062/37 ) :

The 4th and 5th accused were arrested at about 11:30 a.m. 14.6.37 in Room No. 11, the Sing San Xiang (新三祥) Lodging House, No. 495 Canton Road. A search of the room revealed a .25 "VINDIX" Auto. Pistol, No.549 complete with six rounds of ammunition which had been hidden in a table, behind the drawer. On being questioned they stated that the pistol had been supplied by the 16th accused.

12th accused - Possession of Counterfeiting Paraphernalia ( Central Misc. 399/37 ) :

The 12th accused was arrested in Room No.49, the Saung Kiang Lodging House (松江), No.2 Avenue Edward VII French Concession, at about 4:50 p.m. 14.6.37. In his possession were found iron fragments which he stated he was going to deliver to one named Van Ming (范明) at Ninghong for the purpose of making a bomb.

持有6.35毫米“U.P.”牌自动手枪一支，编号4365，子弹九发；以及.38口径西班牙制自动手枪一支，编号12820，子弹六发。他们称这两支手枪是由一名不在押、被称为火子（Dah Fah To，音译）的人给他们的。在最后一名被告的家中还发现了一把铜指节拳套枪。

第4、5和16号被告 - 持有武器及贩卖武器（House 2062/37）：

第4和第5号被告于1937年6月14日上午11时30分许，在广东路495号新三祥（Sing San Xiang）客栈11号房间被捕。搜查房间时，在桌子后面、抽屉背后发现藏有一支.25口径“VINDIX”牌自动手枪，编号549，配有子弹六发。接受讯问时，他们称该手枪由第16号被告提供。

第12号被告 - 持有伪造器具（Central Misc. 399/37）：

第12号被告于1937年6月14日下午4时50分许，在法租界爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII，今延安东路）2号松江（Saung Kiang）客栈49号房间被捕。在他身上发现了铁碎片，他称打算将其交给宁虹（Ninghong，音译）的一名范明（Van Ming）用于制造炸弹。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Detectives visited Van's address situated at No.
11, Loh Dou Tsung 陸家鎮, Dung Wai Hsien 塘灣縣,
near Minghong, but failed to locate this man. At 9:30
a.m. June 17, 1937, a further search of the lodging house
room, where this man was arrested, revealed three plaster
of paris moulds for the manufacture of counterfeit 20cent
pieces.

On being questioned, he stated that these moulds
were left in the room by an unknown man, who is a friend
of Van Ying's.

Three charges will be preferred against the above
mentioned accused on their next appearance before the
Court, whilst an application will be made by the Chinese
authorities for the extradition of all the arrested persons
for investigations concerning their political activities.

D.S.I. Bebenin interviewed Mr. Ru, A/ M.A. during
the afternoon of the 25th. June, 1937, with reference to
the application being made by the Chinese authorities and
to make arrangements to have the case brought before the
Court on the 29th. June, 1937, instead of July 7, 1937.

Mr. Ru stated, that the application should be made
either by the District Court, Nantao, or the S.C.G.P. Bureau
in preference to the Military authorities, as the rendition
agreement had made provisions for extradition to judicial
authorities only.

侦探前往位于塘湾县（Dung Wai Hsien，音译）陆家镇（Loh Dou Tsung，音译）11号、近明虹（Minghong，音译）的范姓地址，但未能找到此人。1937年6月17日上午9时30分，对此人被捕的客栈房间进行进一步搜查，发现了三个用于制造伪造贰角银币的石膏模具。

接受讯问时，他称这些模具是一名不知名男子留在房间的，此人是范英（Van Ying，音译）的朋友。

在上述被告下次出庭时，将对其提出三项指控，同时中国当局将申请引渡所有被捕人员，以调查其政治活动。

1937年6月25日下午，副督察长（D.S.I.）贝别宁（Bebenin，音译）就中国当局提出的申请一事，以及安排将案件于1937年6月29日而非1937年7月7日提交法庭审理事宜，采访了代理助理检察官（A/ M.A.）鲁（Ru，音译）先生。

鲁先生表示，申请应由南市区地方法院或上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.C.G.P. Bureau，此处原文缩写可能有误，通常指SMC或相关司法部门，依语境译为工部局相关部门或保留原意）提出，优于由军方提出，因为移交协定仅规定向司法机关引渡。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The Military authorities have been notified
accordingly, but in spite of this, they state they will
make their own application to the Court.

Mr. Lu has now arranged for this case to be
brought before the Int. Judge's Court on the 29th. June,
1937.

Mention was made in Diary No.5, of the possible
connection of this gang with a murder committed at
Sootow and a robbery committed at 308/5 Sicien Road
( House 569/F ), but further investigations have failed
to bring to light any evidence in respect of these two
cases. Unsuccessful efforts have been made to trace the
man Van King ( 范明 ) through the undermentioned addresses
and telephone numbers found on a piece of paper, seized
in the house of this man at Wuchang : -

Lawyer Van King ( 范明 ).
Office : No.17 Soo Sung Li ( 道生里 ).
Corner of Avenue du Roi Albert, F. C.
and Route Vellon, F. C.
Residence : No.2 Dr. Tuh Pung ( 杜德坊 )
Yung Shing Road ( 永胜路 ), Chapel.
Telephone No. 83035 - H.H.C.10, passage
No.2, House No.5, Rue Chapel, F. C.
Telephone No. 90504 - Liang Yuan Heng
( ), Lane 769, 19 Peking Road.

On the 24th. June, 1937, D.S.I. Coyne forwarded a
further report on the investigations made into the
political activities of this gang. Attached to this
report were statements made by the 6th, 7th, 8th, 11th,
12th, and 17th, accused.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

From the investigations made, there is no doubt
that the criminal element in this gang had been recruited
by the political side to carry out armed robberies and
kidnappings in order to obtain money to finance the
political aims of their party, the plans no doubt being
formulated by the C.C. and 16th. accused.

M. B. Flower
D. I.

根据调查结果，毫无疑问，该团伙中的犯罪成员是被政治派系招募来实施武装抢劫和绑架，以获取资金资助其党派的政治目标，这些计划无疑是由CC系（C.C.，指国民党中统）和第16号被告制定的。

M. B. Flower
